text:
maya: Heads up — we saw a spike of 429s for a high-volume customer earlier, but telemetry shows the router also returned 503s when the edge queue filled. Customer confused which to trust. :thinking:

anil: Can you paste the logs and shed headers? We need to confirm whether those 503s were from node OOM/overload or from explicit early-shed.

maya: logs: `router=router-7 precheck=429 org=acme-key=acct-123 burst_credit=0 queue_len=0` then ~20s later: `router=router-7 queue_overflow=1 reply=503 shed_reason=queue_full`

joel: So we tried precheck (429) when the key hit per-key rate, but when the queue could not accept anything we returned 503. That's expected from current flow, but it mixes signals.

sasha: Mixing is the problem. Apps see a 503 and assume platform outage. 429 communicates throttling and retry semantics. 503 screams "try again later with backoff or contact support" which is bad UX for a quota hit.

kevin: We intentionally used 503 for queue overflow to differentiate capacity vs quota. But agree it's confusing. What if we keep status but add a `x-shed-reason` header and a machine-coded `x-shed-code` so clients can distinguish? e.g. `x-shed-reason: per-key-burst` or `queue-overflow`

maya: That helps. We should also include `retry-after` semantics for 429 where applicable and for 503 only when it's transient (maintenance/oom), otherwise mark as `non-retriable` in the header.

anil: Implementation notes: router already annotates responses with `shed_tag` internally. Proposal: map `shed_tag` -> `x-shed-code` with values: `quota_precheck`, `burst_exhausted`, `queue_full`, `node_overload`. Keep numeric codes too for compactness.

joel: Agreed. Also add telemetry dimension `http_status_vs_shed_code` to the console so we can chart how many queue_fulls are being surfaced as 503 vs 429. Right now dashboards lump them into status codes and it's noisy.

sasha: UX ask: Console should surface per-key burst credits and a small explain panel: "Why did my requests get 503?" Link to docs describing retry/backoff guidance. That will reduce support load.

kevin: Rollout plan: implement headers and telemetry in router, deploy behind a feature flag, canary to 5% of traffic for 24h, watch `errors_by_shed_code`, `client_retry_patterns`, `support_tickets`. If stable, 50% then global.

diana: One more thing — policy for converting 503->429: we could translate queue_full to a 429 with `x-shed-code=queue_full` only if the request is per-key and we detect the key has burst_limits configured. For org-level capacity failures (global pool exhausted) keep 503. That gives apps the best hint.

maya: Love that compromise. Minimizes misinterpretation while preserving signal for true infra outages.

ops-bot: alert: router-7 autoscale triggered (scale-up 2 nodes) at 1945678920

anil: Quick checklist for PR: router: add header mapping + numeric codes, edge-proxy: honor `retry-after` for 429, metrics: emit shed_code label, console: new chart and per-key burst widget, docs: retry guidance. I'll open tickets.

joel: Can we also emit `x-shed-debug` in dev mode with a short token for debugging (not shipped to customers)? Helps SRE repros.

sasha: Good call. Make sure it's scrubbed for PIIs.

kevin: I'll own canary and alerting. If anyone objects, speak now or I'll start the rollout tomorrow. :rocket:

maya: go for it. Thanks all — this should cut down support noise and make routing behavior much clearer. :raised_hands:
